description: Range elements are filtering syntax used after the 'range' keyword in PFC commands. They select subsets of objects (balls, walls, contacts, etc.) based on geometric regions, attributes, or logical conditions.

examples: contact property fric 0.5 range cylinder end-1 0 0 0 end-2 0 0 10 radius 5
notes: Multiple range elements create intersection (AND) by default
Unspecified range affects all objects of target type

Unspecified range affects all objects of target type

UNIFIED-KERNEL caveat (same as FLAC): the 9.x parser enumerates other engines' range elements too (bmaterial/cmodel/deformable/excavated/jmaterial/jmodel/joint-set/interface/structure-type/dfn-3dec/...): accepted by the parser but meaningless for PFC data. They are deliberately not referenced here.

A token the range parser does not know fails the command before anything runs on PFC3D 9.8.54 ('Bad conversion of parameter (nosuch)'); FLAC3D 9.8.54 behaves differently (the range ends and the command runs).

PFC has no 'ball hide' / 'ball select' commands: selected, deselected and use-hidden act on the selection and visibility made in the GUI (with nothing selected, 'selected' chose 0 of 64 balls and 'deselected' all 64).

live_enumeration_pfc3d_98.description: Range-element keyword set listed by 'ball group ... range ?' on PFC3D 9.8.54 (2026-10-31): 66 tokens, identical to the 9.7 enumeration. Every element referenced by this index is in it.

verified_state.selected / deselected: 0 / 64 with nothing selected in the GUI
verified_state.radius: 'radius 0.2' -> 0 balls (2D parameter leaking into the 3D vocabulary)
